properties.name: Temple Mount & Dome of the Rock
properties.subtitle: Old City, Jerusalem
properties.claim: The Herodian platform's largest ashlars — the Western Stone is estimated at several hundred tonnes — plus the Ark of the Covenant described as lethal to touch, are presented as off-world engineering and a powered device.
properties.context: The retaining walls are Herodian (late 1st century BC) with quarries identified within Jerusalem; drafted-margin ashlar is a diagnostic Herodian style found across his projects at Hebron and Caesarea. The Ark's described effects are theological narrative; the object has not been recovered and no engineering inference is available from the texts.
properties.summary: The Temple Mount or al-Haram al-Sharif (Biblical Hebrew: הַר הַבַּיִת, romanized: Har hab-Bayiṯ, Arabic: الحَرَم الشَّرِيف, romanized: al-Ḥaram aš-Šarīf or الأَقْصَى, al-Aqṣā) is an elevated plateau in the Old City of Jerusalem that comprises the Islamic religious compound known as al-Aqsa, which includes the al-Aqsa Mosque and the Dome of the Rock. Historically the location of two successive Jewish temples, the area has been venerated as a holy site for thousands of years including in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
